newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL SAYS FUEL SALES NORMAL DESPITE PROBE.
newsitem.headline: MOL SAYS FUEL SALES NORMAL DESPITE PROBE.

text.p: Hungarian oil and gas company MOL Rt said on Tuesday petrol retailers are continuing to buy fuel from the company despite alleged quality problems in some north Hungarian counties.
"I just received confirmation that all of our partners are continuing to buy the merchandise (petrol)," Istvan Nadassy, MOL's director in charge of refining told Reuters.

Press reports said on Monday that after a series of problems with car fuel pumps around the north-east Hungarian city of Miskolc, the Hungarian unit of German service station group Aral decided to buy petrol from Austria until MOL solves the problem.
MOL said that the quality of its petrol meets Hungarian standards but that it will take two weeks to complete an investigation into the causes of the reported problem.
MOL added that it will supply the north Hungarian region with petrol from its Szazhalombatta refinery. Normally the region receives its petrol from MOL's Tiszai refinery.
Nadassy added that while MOL will incur extra costs due to the different supply route, the costs would be marginal.
"It is certain that the extra cost will be minimal," he said.
Nadassy said that despite press reports to the contrary, the Tiszai refinery had not been closed down for the duration of the investigation.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, MOL shares stood at 4,645 forints, up 185, at 1003 GMT.
